detail.recordsHeadingGeneric: Add these records at your DNS provider

groups.trackingNote: Tracking links use the default host — no DNS records needed. Set a custom subdomain in Configuration to serve them from your own domain.
groups.trackingNoteDefaultOnly: Tracking links use the default host — no DNS records needed.

tracking.openHint: Injects a 1×1 transparent pixel with a unique reference, served from your tracking subdomain, so a person rendering it counts as an open. Fetches a mail client or security scanner made before anyone looked are recorded as prefetched and never count; blocked images and plain-text sends are still missed.
tracking.clickHint: Rewrites each link to redirect through your tracking subdomain, then sends the recipient on to the original destination URL.
tracking.subdomainHint: Both the click redirect and the open pixel are served from this subdomain of your own domain, instead of the shared default host. Add the CNAME below and verify it.
tracking.subdomainError: Use a single lowercase DNS label.
tracking.subdomainReturnPathClash: The tracking subdomain must be different from the return-path subdomain.
tracking.subdomainUnavailable: This deployment cannot serve tracking links from your own domain right now, so the subdomain below is not in use — emails ship with their original links and no open pixel. Clear it to remove the setting.
tracking.localWarning: Tracking needs a publicly reachable URL. This deployment's APP_BASE_URL is local, so recipients can never reach the tracked links or the open pixel — the toggles stay off until a public URL is configured.
tracking.cloudRequiresSubdomain: Tracked links here are served only from your own tracking subdomain — a shared tracking host is what ad blockers and spam filters learn to block. Without one, emails ship with their original links and no open pixel.
tracking.confirmEnable:
New mail from this domain will emit {kind} events.

Mail already sent stays as it is — your webhooks and metrics pick up the new events right away.
tracking.confirmDisable:
New mail from this domain will stop emitting {kind} events.

Events already recorded stay; your webhooks and metrics simply stop receiving new ones.

configuration.subdomainNeutral: Using the default tracking host. Set a subdomain to serve links from your own domain.
configuration.tlsHint: Opportunistic attempts a secure TLS connection and falls back to plaintext if the receiving server doesn't support it. Enforced requires TLS — the message is never sent unencrypted.

detail.checkDnsTooltip: Re-reads live DNS for every record and refreshes the SES verification status. Live results catch a record you just removed; SES can lag before it de-verifies a domain whose records are gone.
detail.dnsOnlyHint: On Cloudflare, keep the proxy off for this record (grey cloud, "DNS only"). A proxied CNAME answers with Cloudflare's addresses instead of this target, and TLS for this host is served by MillionSend.
detail.inheritedDmarc: No record at this name. Receivers fall back to {from} (p={policy}), which already covers this subdomain.
detail.foundAwaitingProvider: Record found in DNS; awaiting the provider's confirmation (usually minutes, up to 72 hours).
detail.aiPrompt:
Add these DNS records to the domain {domain} at my DNS provider, then check each record has propagated:

{records}
detail.bannerLookingBody: This may take a few hours depending on {provider}'s propagation time.
detail.bannerLookingBodyGeneric: This may take a few hours depending on your DNS provider's propagation time.
detail.deleteBody: This permanently deletes the domain and its DNS configuration. Sending from it stops immediately.
detail.deleteError: Couldn't delete the domain. Try again.

setup.title: Set up tracking
setup.subtitle: Click and open events are served from a subdomain of your own domain, so ad blockers and spam filters do not recognise a shared tracking host. Add its CNAME and verify it.

receiving.note: Receives mail for the addresses of its inboxes and, with Catch-all on, for every other address at {domain}. Read it under Inboxes, through the API or with the email.received webhook.
receiving.noteApex: Receives mail for the addresses of its inboxes (every address with Catch-all on), and its MX record brings all of the domain's mail here. If people already get email at {domain}, use a subdomain such as {example} so their mailboxes stay as they are.
receiving.notVerified: Available once the domain is verified.
receiving.confirmEnable: Once the MX record points here, mail to the addresses of the inboxes at {domain} is accepted and stored here. Other addresses are refused until you turn on Catch-all.
receiving.confirmEnableApex: Once the MX record points here, mail to the addresses of the inboxes at {domain} is accepted and stored here, and the domain's mail stops reaching the mailboxes that get it today. Other addresses are refused until you turn on Catch-all.
receiving.confirmDisable: Mail sent to {domain} is refused from now on. Emails already received stay until the retention window removes them.
receiving.errorNotVerified: Verify the domain before turning on receiving.
receiving.errorTaken: Another team already receives mail for {domain}.
receiving.summaryCatchAll: {count, plural, one {# inbox} other {# inboxes}} + catch-all
receiving.catchAllHint: Mail to addresses without an inbox lands in All received. Off: those addresses are refused.
receiving.catchAllOffConfirm: Mail to addresses at {domain} that have no inbox is refused from now on. Inbox addresses keep receiving.

limit.note: New domains start small because inbox providers are wary of mail from them. The limit grows on its own, and steady clean sending lifts it sooner. Mail over the day's limit waits and goes out the next day. A higher plan doesn't change it.
limit.noteUnknown: New domains start small because inbox providers are wary of mail from them. We couldn't find when this domain was registered, so steady clean sending is what lifts the limit. Mail over the day's limit waits and goes out the next day. A higher plan doesn't change it.
